Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's it from us for this match. It wasn't quite a classic but South Africa would take that win all day long. Now the attention shifts to the Test series, where a notable absentee is AB de Villiers. The first Test is in Dunedin which starts from Wednesday, 8th March, 2017, at 1100 local time (2200 GMT, previous night). South Africa whitewashed Sri Lanka at home while the Kiwis defeated Bangladesh 2-0 here. It promises to be a good series. In the meanwhile, you can catch all the action from the second India-Australia Test. Until then, Adios! Take Care!

South African skipper, AB DE VILLIERS says winning a lot of tosses made it a lot easier (South Africa won 5 out of 5 tosses in the series). Says New Zealand played good cricket the whole series. Credits the batting team for a fantastic effort. Reckons the pitch was a bit slower and informs that finding gaps was difficult. Thinks his bowlers took wickets at regular intervals to put New Zealand under pressure. Says that Faf du Plessis and David Miller played fantastic knocks. Calls Faf a great player and informs that the talk at the centre (when he and Faf were batting) was to stay in the middle. Admits that he's going to miss the Test series but wishes luck for the boys and mentions that he'll enjoy the series from home.

New Zealand skipper, KANE WILLIAMSON admits that it was a disappointing effort with the bat, Praises the Proteas and feels they totally deserve the series win. Is proud of the way his team fielded tonight. Feels that the batting needed to put up some more runs on the board and 150 was definitely not enough. Aims to continue improvement by assessing their performance against the top sides. Is happy after a terrific home summer but still wishes for that one big performance which could have got them the trophy. Wants his side to move up the ODI rankings.

KAGISO RABADA has been named the MAN OF THE MATCH. He says that he just tried to get some rest a day before so that he could be fresh today. Admits that it was tough to play the short ball on this pitch and they utilized it to their advantage. Is looking forward to transform from ODI cricket to Test cricket in the upcoming series.

In spite of the constant pressure, Faf du Plessis held his own and was well supported by David Miller's 45 that came at a strike rate of 128.57 as the pair assured that they regain the numero uno status in ODIs. Coming to the Kiwi bowlers, it was a stupendous effort from them. Everyone contributed here and there. Had the runs been a little more, there could've been a twist. Stay tuned for the presentation.

It still seemed like that it was South Africa's game but the wickets of Jean-Paul Duminy and captain AB de Villiers, who was sent back to the hut because of a ripper from Jimmy Neesham, made the match more interesting than it should've been. Williamson followed McCullum's school of captaincy as he never let go of the aggressive field settings and maintained pressure on the Proteas.

Not quite a Grant Elliott kind of six, but a four from Faf du Plessis sealed the match and the series for the South Africans. A match that they ideally should've won easily, but some smart captaincy and outstanding bowling from the Kiwi bowlers made life difficult for the Proteas. It all started because of de Kock's brain fade as he fell prey to Jeetan Patel, who opened the bowling for the hosts. From there on, a flurry of dot balls from the Black Caps made Hashim Amla play a false shot and depart.

FOUR! Those are the winning runs! What a way to finish the game. Banged in short outside off, du Plessis is back in a flash and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. That brings up Faf's half century as well and SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY 6 WICKETS, TAKING THE 5-MATCH SERIES 3-2!

TOP EDGE, DROPPED! That should have been taken. A short ball around off, goes for the pull but gets a top edge. The ball goes high in the air and Jeetan Patel comes running in from fine leg. He gets to the ball, dives forward, takes the catch but as soon as the hand makes contact with the ground, the ball spills out. A single taken. Patel shakes his head.
Slides on with the arm, pitching around off, Faf is rooted in his crease and misses his flick, getting hit on the pads. Santner appeals for LBW but then bails out. Missing leg.
Pushes this towards mid on now.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, Miller heaves it to the leg side but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat towards mid on. A run taken.
Goes back and works it through the leg side for a single.
Landed around off, watchfully defended.
MITCHELL SANTNER comes back for the final rites.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
A low full toss on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
FOUR! This is class batting. On a length outside off, du Plessis eases this through the covers and gets a boundary. Only 8 more needed now.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. Southee finishes with 10-1-40-0. New Zealand would have dearly loved a couple of wickets.
Fifty run stand comes up between Faf du Plessis and David Miller off 47 balls. It is the first 50-run stand of the match. Miller has scored 43 off those. Talk about leading from the front.
SIX! Ho ho ho! What a shot! Amazing batsmanship. A length ball on middle, Miller swings it cleanly over long on!
FOUR! CRASH! Miller is in a hurry now. Jumps down the track, Southee reacts by pitching it short, but Miller is upto it and clubs it past the bowler to the fence down the ground. 18 more needed now.
A short ball outside off, Miller pulls it through mid-wicket but the fielder inside the ring stops it well.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a run.
Works it down the leg side for a single.
Stays back in his crease and defends.
The batsman opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man. They pick up a single.

FOUR! Short and wide outside off, easily put away through the covers off the back foot via a nice punch. Miller moves to 31 from 25 balls. Guess the time for miracles has gone by. The Proteas are cruising.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
FOUR! In the air... but safe. Full and wide outside off, Miller plays this a bit loosely but gets it over cover for a boundary. 29 more needed now. The stand is worth 33 from 38 balls.
A short ball around middle, Miller sways out of the way.
TRENT BOULT is back on.
Outside off, played straight to point.
TOP EDGE, SAFE! A short ball around off, David looks to pull but gets a top edge which does not carry to Colin de Grandhomme running in from deep mid-wicket. A run taken.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
A short ball around off, cuts back in, Faf plays a pull shot like an afterthought towards fine leg for a run. Moves to 40 now.

Full and outside off, Miller leans and drives it wide of mid off. Jeetan Patel gets across to his right, slides but fumbles. The batsmen take a single, Faf wants one on the misfield but Patel recovers quickly and Miller sends  his partner back.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards deep square leg. The call is for two but they can get only one.
Down the leg side, tickled straight to short fine leg.
Around off, worked through mid on for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.

FOUR! Overcompensates does Patel, by firing it down the leg side. Miller just tickles it to the fine leg fence. 39 more to win now. The stand is worth 23 from 27 balls while Miller is now on 20 from 16 deliveries.
SIX! CRACK! When he hits, they say hit! Terrific shot. Full and outside off, Miller comes forward and dispatches this right onto the top of the sight screen.
Full and outside off, defended towards cover.
JEETAN PATEL is back on.
Outside off, steered to third man for a single. 49 more needed for a win now. Miller moves to 10 from 13 balls.
Outside off, driven straight to mid off.

ALMOST A CATCH! FOUR! Full and wide outside off, Miller looks to drive but gets a thickish outside edge. The ball flies in the air, but goes just wide of a diving Jimmy Neesham at backward point. Mitchell Santner gives it a chase from short extra cover and so does Dean Brownlie from third man. Santner dives near the ropes with Brownlie almost near him and they nearly collide. Brownlie has to dive over Santner to avoid getting hurt but still gets hit on the head a touch. Thankfully, both players are fine. 100 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA! The stand is worth 12 from 22 balls.
A sharp bouncer outside off, David looks to pull but is beaten by pace. The short ball has been effective from both teams tonight.
Full and straight, defended towards mid-wicket.
Another brilliant piece of fielding. Full and around off, Miller drives it through the covers but Mitchell Santner at short extra cover dives full length to his right to stop it.
TIM SOUTHEE is back on now. Williamson rotating his bowlers. He needs wickets. Not 1, not 2, but 6. This Protea batting line-up is long.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
A short ball now, outside off, comfortably pulled through mid-wicket for a run.
Good fielding again. Full and around off, driven towards mid off but Boult throws himself to his right and stops it cleanly.
Back of a length outside off, extra bounce, Miller gets on top of it and fends it down on the off side.
This is on a good length around off, pushed towards point.
On a good length outside off, chopped down to third man for a single.

LBW shout, but nothing in it. Pitched outside leg, David is way down the track as he looks to flick but misses. The ball goes off his pads towards first slip who even has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Miller was in though.
FOUR! CLOUT! That eases the pressure. Short and outside off, Miller gets on top of it and punches it through the covers for a boundary. Nice way to get off the mark. 56 needed for a win now.
Captain and bowler have a chat...
Landed outside off, du Plessis gets on top of the bounce and dabs it to third man for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, solidly defended.
On a good length outside off, driven straight to mid off.
On a good length outside off, Miller looks to defend but the ball stays low and goes off the bottom part of the bat towards mid-wicket. Good follow-up to the excellent over from Neesham.
EDGED, SAFE! Full and wide outside off, Faf throws his bat at it and gets a thick outside edge which flies over point towards third man. A single taken.

Excellent fielding! New Zealand are giving it their all in the field. On a length outside off, du Plessis punches this on the up through the covers but Mitchell Santner dives to his left at short extra cover and stops the ball. Brilliant.
Around off, this time Faf covers the line and blocks.
Landed around off, du Plessis is squared up a touch and somehow squirts the ball towards point.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Williamson gets his strike bowler back. Here is TRENT BOULT.
DAVID MILLER walks in at number 6, replacing his captain.

OUT! That is a snorter! Is the game still alive? This was a plan which was going on for the last 15 minutes or so. Only the execution was not proper. This time though, the ball landed on target. Neesham darted in a bouncer outside off and de Villiers who was already on the front foot, had nowhere to go. He tried to get out of the way but could not keep his hands out. The ball kissed his gloves and lobbed to Luke Ronchi who did the rest. Neesham is pumped up. Why not? Auckland is a place for miracles. Just 62 runs needed but if the Kiwis get a wicket or two quickly, who knows....
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a run.
Down the leg side, flicked through square leg for a couple.
WIDE. That is yet another slower bouncer going over the bowler's head. Only this time, the bowler is different.
Outside off, Faf pushes but misses.
Outside off, dabbed towards third man for a single.
Full and outside off, defended to the off side.
JIMMY NEESHAM comes back on to bowl.
Outside off, defended to the off side.
WIDE. Another attempted slower ball, this is a bouncer, but goes a mile over Faf's head.
Fractionally short in length outside off, punched straight to cover.
Full and around middle, defended to the leg side.
WIDE. Attempted slower ball goes awry, slips it down the leg side, Faf misses his flick too.
On a good length now, down the leg side, nudged fine for a run. Just 69 more needed now.
Banged in short, pulled towards deep square leg for a single.
Full and on middle and leg, defended towards short mid-wicket.
Drinks have been called.
Loops this one around off, ABD drives it back to the bowler.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.

SIX! Bowls this a tad short and gets punished. ABD camps back and pulls it hard over mid-wicket. This is the kind of intent that South Africa needs right now. They shouldn't allow New Zealand into the game and that is exactly what ABD is trying to do with these timely risks.
Shorter and flatter, ABD makes room and cuts it towards covers.
Tosses this one outside off, Faf eases it down to long off for a single.
Flatter delivery, Faf flicks it towards the leg side.
Mitchell Santner comes into the bowling attack for the first time today!
FOUR! ABD comes down the track and tries to go over mid off. He miscues and the ball goes towards third man for a boundary. Risky shot that!
Short of a length ball, ABD looks to upper cut but misses.
CDG bangs this short and the ball goes over his head. Umpire gives a warning but it looked like a wide.
On a length outside off, de Villiers drives it towards covers.
Length ball around off, ABD stays in his crease and blocks it.

To call this phase a struggle for the South Africans would be an understatement! Length ball outside off, Faf pushes it towards covers and looks for a run. He was hesitant a bit but ABD wanted it. Santner runs to his right from covers and makes a one handed throw at striker's end but misses. Close shave that!
Colin de Grandhomme is back into the attack.
Shorter delivery, ABD swivels and pulls it straight to backward square leg.
SIX! ABD dances down the track and slams this tossed up delivery over long on for a maximum. The boundary was short but it wouldn't have mattered as it was deep into the stands!
Floated delivery, on middle, Faf flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

NOT OUT!  Reprieve for the visitors but What is South Africa doing here? Tossed up delivery around middle, Faf comes forward to defend but misses and gets rapped on the pads. New Zealand appeal and the umpire obliges. Faf reviews after a chat with ABD. The replays suggest that it was missing and the South African survives.
South Africa review for a LBW.
Tosses this one around off, du Plessis punches it towards mid-wicket.
Shortish delivery, around off, ABD gets on his toes and pushes it towards the off side.
Length ball on the sticks, Faf knocks it towards mid on and sets off instantly. AB obliges. The mid on fielder was a bit slow there and they complete the single easily.
Back of a length delivery, chest height, AB hops and tucks it away towards backward square leg for a single.
On a length outside off, Faf opens the face of the bat and guides it to third man. One run added to the total!
Length ball outside off, Faf leaves it alone.

FOUR! Over pitched and duly punished. Absolute beauty of a shot from Faf. Picture perfect. Drives it down the ground with straight face of the bat. The mid off and mid on fielders had no chance as the ball goes reaches the fence in a whisker.
WIDE! Bowls this down the leg side as Faf misses his flick. Extra run for the Proteas.
ABD looks to reverse sweep this tossed up delivery, but misses. Jeetan appeals for a LBW, the umpire is not interested.
FOUR! Sprays this down the leg side, ABD tickles it away with soft hands for a boundary to fine leg. What a way to get off the mark!
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
ABD punches this floated delivery off the back foot.
AB de Villiers is the next man in.

OUT! If there is one word that aptly describes Duminy it is loose! Tossed up delivery outside off, a casual drive by JP goes straight to Santner at covers who is more than happy to catch it. The ploy to give Duminy more time at the top hasn't worked. Another poor outing for the southpaw. Three wickets have fallen, are we in for something here?
Quicker delivery, Duminy knocks it back to the bowler.
WIDE! Starts his second spell with a wide. Flatter delivery down the leg side, Duminy misses his flick.
Jeetan Patel comes back into the attack!
Good length ball outside off, Duminy steers it down to third man for a single.
Good length ball, outside off, Duminy stays in his crease and pats it towards point.
Bowls this outside off, Duminy throws his bat at it and misses.
Fullish delivery, Faf pushes it towards the bowler. The ball hits Southee's hand and goes towards mid off. They run a single.

FOUR! Much needed for South Africa. The dot balls were stacking up and it was necessary to put one away. And Faf does that with elegance. Length ball, outside off, Faf drives it with ease past the cover fielders as the ball rolls away to the fence.
Bowls this outside off, Faf taps it towards point.
Lands this on a length, fourth stump line, JP knocks it towards the mid off fielder.
Length ball, outside off, Duminy moves across and pushes it down the ground.
Straighter delivery on the pads, Duminy flicks it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Length delivery, outside off, Faf opens the face of the bat and guides it through point for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Angles in a length delivery, around leg, du Plessis tickles it fine. Jeetan Patel hares across from third man slides and saves two runs for his side. Two runs added to the total!
Bowls a full toss. Duminy pats it towards the point region.
Leg bye! Back of a length delivery, hip height, Faf hops, looks to tuck but it hits his pad and goes towards backward square leg. They take a leg bye.
Length ball, around middle and leg, Faf knocks it towards mid on.
Bowls this slightly fuller which is swinging away, Faf gets forward and drives it towards covers.
Angles in a length ball, FdP pushes it towards covers.
Length ball which stays low, however Faf gets in a good position crouches a touch to defend it.
Fullish delivery around off, Duminy drives it to mid off.
Jean-Paul Duminy comes out to replace Hashim Amla.

OUT! This was coming. The pressure was building and the South African batsmen were clearly struggling. Length ball, around off, Amla drives it with total control though directly to Santner at covers who reverse cups it. The dot balls have handed the wicket to New Zealand.
Good length delivery, fifth stump line, Amla comes down wanting to go over covers but misses. A horrendous shot!
Wide! Amla looks to flick but this goes down the leg side.
On a length around off, Faf lofts it unconvincingly over mid off and runs one.
Length ball around off, du Plessis offers a front foot defense.
Bowls a fuller delivery, Faf drives it down the ground as the ball hits Amla's bat and goes towards mid off.
Bowling change! Colin de Grandhomme is into the attack.
Marginally ahead of length, around off. Amla goes on the back foot to defend but gets beaten on the outside edge because of the extra bounce.
Angles in a length ball, Amla drives it towards mid off.
Wide! Strays it down the leg, Amla looks to tuck it away but it goes past him.
Good length delivery, outside off, Amla drives it perfectly. But it goes directly to the fielder.
Bowls a length delivery, Amla looks to drive but gets beaten.
On a length, around off, Amla defends it solidly.
Length ball around middle ang leg, Amla pushes it down the ground.
Powerplay two has been signalled!
4 Leg byes. Sprays this down the leg side, Faf looks to tickle it fine but it hits his pads and goes between the leg slip and the keeper for four byes.

FOUR! Boult bangs this short, Faf swivels a bit and pulls this hard to deep mid-wicket for a boundary. Easy pickings those. Seems like Faf is sick of these shortish deliveries and has decided to put them away.
Length ball outside off, Faf leaves it alone.
WIDE! Bowls this way outside off, out of Faf's reach. Will have to bowl that one again.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Short of a length around off, Faf gets across and blocks it towards covers.
NASTY! Back of a length delivery which comes back sharply. Faf is caught on the back foot and the ball goes onto hit the inside of his thigh.
Full delivery nips back in, Amla moves across a touch and just drives it to mid on.
Length delivery on the pads, Amla whips it with soft hands towards square leg.
Back of a length delivery, mounts very high, Amla swivels across and pulls it in front of square. They run a couple.
Angles in a length ball, Amla reads it early, stays in the crease to defend it.
Bowls a good length ball around off, Amla goes forward and pushes it towards covers.
Lands this on a length outside off, gives Amla no reason to play at it.

FOUR! Fullish delivery, on the fourth stump line, Faf strides forward and just places it through covers. The cover fielder dives but the ball evades him and rolls away to the fence for a boundary. Classy shot that!
Good length delivery, around off, Amla moves across to push it towards covers but it takes the outside edge and goes to third man. They run a single.
Short of a length ball, nips back in, Amla shuffles across and whips it to mid-wicket.
On a length just outside off, Faf taps it towards third man for an easy single.
Length delivery around middle and leg, Faf defends it towards the leg side.
Back of a length delivery, angling in, raps Faf on the pads.
Faf drives it this length delivery towards covers where the fielder dives to make a stop. One run added to the total!
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Bowls a full ball outside off, du Plessis knocks it to mid off.
Full delivery on the pads, Faf flicks it to mid-wicket where the fielder makes a sharp save.
Fullish delivery, swinging away, du Plessis leans forward and drives it down the ground.
Bowls a length ball outside off, FdP leaves it alone.
Welcome back. The players are out on the field. South Africa will aim to play normal cricket and seal the series. Here is Southee.

Not a bad mini-session for New Zealand. They got the ball moving and managed to get rid of de Kock. 150 should not be too much of an ask for the Proteas but at least the Kiwis have something to smile about in the break. They have a long, tall mountain to climb, if they are to put this dominant Protea side under pressure. Join us back at 1815 local (0515 GMT).
Outside off, left alone. DINNER BREAK!
Banged in short, pulled through square leg for a single.
Angled into the right-hander from around the wicket, FdP watches it sail through.
A short ball outside off, du Plessis thinks about the pull but then bails out.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, Faf reaches out and then aims to drive, or swing it through the leg side, not quite sure. In the end, gets beaten.
We will have one more over before the break.
Outside off, the overeager FdP reaches out for it and dabs it towards third man for a single.
Flashy from Faf. Full and wide outside off, du Plessis looks to drive but there is some away swing available and he is beaten. Tentative, tentative.
On a good length this time, outside off, tapped towards point.
Outside off, played with an angled bat towards point.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
A short ball around off, Faf looks to pull but gets a bottom edge back to the bowler.
TIM SOUTHEE to bowl now. This could possibly be the final over before the break.
Landed well outside off, angling in, HA gets a big stride forward and shoulders arms.
Outside off, tapped to the off side.
WIDE. Angles this down the leg side, Hashim misses his flick.
Gets across his stumps and looks to flick but misses. Seems like he got an inside edge from the reaction of the bowler.
Outside off, left alone.
Boult switches the angle to around the wicket now.
FOUR! What a shot. Full and outside off, Amla leans and drives this through the covers. That races away.
Full and just around off, watchfully defended.
Full on middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
On a good length around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
On middle and leg watchfully defended.
Skipper Faf du Plessis walks in at number 3, replacing de Kock.

OUT! De Kock departs! Flighted outside off, de Kock comes down the track and looks to go over the top. However, he is not to the pitch of the ball and miscues it. The ball goes in the air and seems to be evading mid off but Kane Williamson runs back from inside the circle, keeps his eyes on the ball and takes a spectacular catch. Patel gets Quinnie again.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
Stays back in his crease and defends.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
FOUR! HANDSOME! Full and outside off, de Kock leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary! He is away and running.
On a length outside off, driven on the up towards point.
TRENT BOULT will bowl with the other new ball.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full on middle, swept powerfully towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
That's hit the batsman on his pads.
Goes back and works it through square leg.

Huge LBW shout! The arm ball around leg stump, Quinton stays back again, does not move his feet, tries to work it to the leg side but misses and is hit on the pads. Patel appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Williamson asks about the review but Patel himself indicates that it was too high.
Landed outside off, de Kock stays back and pushes it towards cover.
The players are out in the middle to play a couple of overs before lunch. Surprisingly Jeetan Patel will bowl with the new ball. QDK and Amla too have arrived at the crease!
